title: Cold rebuild: Compress an address
summary: Rebuild Compress an address from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Compress an address** in *IPv6 basics*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: `IPAddress` prints IPv6 in canonical short form. What does this print?
steps.explain: Leading zeros go, and the longest zero run becomes `::`.

steps.title: Rebuild Compress an address cold
prompt: Write `string Compress(string full)` producing the canonical form from 8 full groups: drop leading zeros (a group of zeros becomes `0`),
then replace the **longest** run of two or more zero groups with `::` (the first run on a tie). Don't use `IPAddress`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
